Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `main` at `edba1e362fa6f4e6b6052310b14d9a77fd7870b7`. The `Integration branch mismatch:` line reads `unknown`, not `true`, so planning goes ahead.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`
- `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`
- `changelog.d/unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md` (new)

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_nothing_to_implement_closes_without_a_fixup_wait red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_nothing_to_implement_closes_after_an_earlier_done_wait red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_nothing_to_implement_no_wait_keeps_the_judge_otherwise
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_nothing_to_implement_no_wait_posts_the_marker_once
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_nothing_to_implement_close_keeps_the_resume_otherwise
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: unblock judge behaviour is fully covered by fake-gh unit tests; production only shows it when a matching blocked issue appears.

## What the code does today (read on this ref)
- `unblock_nothing_to_implement_close <fixup> <done text> <tracking>` is at `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` lines ~572-627. It checks, in order:
  - the kill switch;
  - `ITEM_KIND=issue`, `ITEM_STOP=blocked`, and an empty tracking issue;
  - a jq check on `${RUNTIME_DIR}/item_comments.json` that the newest trusted "Planning blocked: human input required." comment has the line `Reason: <UNBLOCK_NOTHING_TO_IMPLEMENT_REASON>`, with no trusted implementation plan after it.
  
  It then builds the marker `<!-- ai:unblock-nothing-to-implement:v1 item=N fixup=F -->` and makes at most three writes (comment, `ai:closed` label, close as completed). It logs `op=nothing_to_implement outcome=closed|skip reason=...`.
- Its only call site is in `unblock_main`, inside the fix-up-wait-done branch (~line 2008, comment `# #8470: ...`), after the operator-step escalation and the hold.
- After the fix-up-wait block, `unblock_main` runs these in order:
  1. Q129 check-triage close.
  2. Q148 heal-already-fixed close.
  3. The hold block (an open hold returns, an expired one falls through).
  4. The #9484 operator-escalation park (returns while unresolved).
  5. The deterministic exits: scope re-grant, then the Q56 blocked-fix-up escalation, which always returns.
  6. Evidence, fingerprint, the model verdict and the CRITICAL escalation.
  
  The #9215 failure happened on this last stretch: the wait was already `done` (03:49Z), the block came later (07:46Z), and nothing in steps 1-5 matched.

## Functions or modules to implement
1. Change `unblock_nothing_to_implement_close` in `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`. The signature, name and return contract stay the same. Add one optional 4th argument:
   - Signature becomes `<fixup> <done text> <tracking> [<block after>]`.
   - Empty `fixup` means there is no fix-up. Set a local `fixup_label="${fixup:-none}"` and use it in every `unblock_log` line (`fixup=none`) and in the marker `<!-- ai:unblock-nothing-to-implement:v1 item=${ITEM} fixup=none -->`.
   - The block-after argument goes into the existing jq check as `--arg after "${4:-}"`. The final expression becomes `$block.match and ($plan == "" or $plan < $block.at) and ($after == "" or $block.at > $after)`. The newest block must be newer than the given timestamp. Every existing check (trusted login, newest block, reason line, no later plan, standalone, kill switch) stays as it is.
   - Comment text when `fixup` is empty: "Closing as completed: planning found nothing to implement for this issue (`<reason>`), and no fix-up is pending. A resume command would only stop planning again, so the unblock judge closed the issue instead. Reopen it and reply with `/reclarify` if work is still missing." The marker follows on its own line. The text with a fix-up does not change.
   - Duplicate-marker check when `fixup` is empty: a trusted copy of the `fixup=none` marker counts only if its `created_at` is at or after the newest block's `created_at`. A re-block after a reopen then gets its own comment. The duplicate check on the fix-up path does not change.
   - Update the header comment block for the function to describe the no-wait caller and the 4th argument. Also update the `UNBLOCK_NOTHING_TO_IMPLEMENT_CLOSE_ENABLED` doc lines at the top of the file (lines ~70-72): the switch also turns off the no-wait close.
2. Add a new call site in `unblock_main`, right after the deterministic-exits block (scope re-grant and Q56 `unblock_fixup_origin`/`unblock_escalate_fixup`) and before `# Evidence and fingerprint.`:
   ```
   # #9518: a nothing-to-implement block with no pending fix-up wait is closed too.
   if [ "${ITEM_KIND}" = "issue" ] && unblock_nothing_to_implement_close "" "" "${tracking}" "${wait:+${wait_updated:-}}"; then
       return 0
   fi
   ```
   - The 4th argument is `wait_updated` (the newest wait comment's `updated_at`) when a wait exists, and empty otherwise. A wait that was open goes no further than here only when it ended in this same run as "did not merge in time". Its block is the one the judge already filed a fix-up for, so it is older than the wait. That block stays with the judge, as today.
   - Use `${wait_updated:-}`: `wait_updated` is declared `local` without a value and the script runs under `set -u`.
   - On return 0 (closed, or a write failed) the run stops. Nothing else needs retrying: the scan picks the still-blocked issue up again on the next tick, and the marker is not posted twice.

## Data structures affected
- New marker variant: `<!-- ai:unblock-nothing-to-implement:v1 item=<n> fixup=none -->`. It uses the same prefix and version, so the existing marker family stays recognisable.
- Log line: the existing `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item= kind= stop= fixup= op=nothing_to_implement outcome=closed|skip reason=...` with the value `fixup=none`. No new log key or prefix.
- No new env var. The existing `UNBLOCK_NOTHING_TO_IMPLEMENT_CLOSE_ENABLED` (default `true`) controls both paths.

## API or interface changes
- No new GitHub API reads. The check uses only `${RUNTIME_DIR}/item_comments.json`, which is already fetched. Writes are at most the same three (comment, label, close). The no-wait path has no wait-comment patch.
- The shell function takes an optional 4th argument. The existing caller passes three arguments, so it keeps the current behaviour exactly.

Data flow:
1. The scan dispatches the judge for an `ai:blocked` standalone issue. `unblock_main` reads the item and its comments (existing reads).
2. A fix-up wait that is pending returns early, as today. A wait that is done, or no wait at all, falls through.
3. Q129, Q148, hold and escalation run as today. Then the Q56 fix-up-origin escalation runs as today.
4. New: `unblock_nothing_to_implement_close "" "" tracking wait_updated` closes the issue and the run returns.
5. Otherwise the evidence, fingerprint and model verdict run as today.

Failure modes:
- A comment, label or close write fails. The run logs `fixup=none op=nothing_to_implement outcome=skip reason=<x>_failed` and returns 0. The next scan tick retries, and the marker is not posted again because the newer trusted marker is found.
- The jq check fails or the comments are malformed. The function returns 1 and the judge runs as today (fail open toward the existing behaviour).

## Decisions
### D1 — Place the no-wait call after the Q56 fix-up-origin exit
- Chosen: insert after the deterministic-exits block and before the evidence and fingerprint step.
- Alternatives considered: right after the fix-up-wait block, before Q129, Q148, hold and escalation; or before the Q56 fix-up-origin escalation.
- Why: open holds and operator escalations keep their parking semantics. A blocked fix-up keeps its Q56 escalation; closing it here would end the parent's wait as "did not merge" instead of escalating. This is the last point before the model verdict and the CRITICAL alert, which is where #9215 failed.

### D2 — Require the block to be newer than an existing wait
- Chosen: pass `wait_updated` as a "block after" bound when any wait exists.
- Alternatives considered: no bound (close whenever the newest block matches).
- Why: when a fix-up closed without merging or timed out in this run, its block is the one the judge filed the fix-up for. That decision stays with the judge, as today. #9215 (block 07:46Z after the wait finished at 03:49Z) still closes. This only adds a check (§6 Correctness > Speed).

### D3 — `fixup=none` value instead of a new marker name
- Chosen: the same `ai:unblock-nothing-to-implement:v1` marker with `fixup=none`, as the issue's constraint asks.
- Alternatives considered: a new marker name such as `...-no-wait:v1`.
- Why: the existing marker family stays recognisable, and no fix-up is referenced when there is none.

### D4 — No agents.d fragment
- Chosen: describe the behaviour in the changelog fragment and in code comments only.
- Alternatives considered: an `agents.d/9518-...md` fragment for "Integration-sync verifier + bootstrap contract" or "Stable log prefixes".
- Why: the issue's `files_touched` scope does not cover the agents file, so a fragment would trip the scope lock. The log key set is unchanged; only the value `none` is new.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: issue comments are untrusted. A close needs the newest "Planning blocked" comment to come from the pipeline login (`UNBLOCK_LOGIN`) with the exact reason line. An implementation-plan comment posted later by a bot, OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, or by the pipeline login, prevents the close. Non-trusted users cannot forge the block or the duplicate marker, because the marker check also requires the pipeline login.
- Abuse case: a user posts a fake "Planning blocked … nothing to implement" comment to get an issue closed. The trusted-login check rejects it (covered by the `untrusted_block` test).
- Abuse case: an orchestrator child forges standalone status. Tracking
